title: Factors, Multiples & Primes
description: Finding factors and multiples, identifying prime numbers, using prime factorisation, and finding HCF and LCM.

notes.heading: Factors and Multiples
notes.body: A factor is a whole number that divides exactly into another number. For example, factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24. A multiple is the result of multiplying a number by a whole number. Multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, ... A common mistake is mixing them up: factors are small or equal to the number, multiples are larger or equal.

notes.heading: Prime Numbers
notes.body: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. The first few primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19. Note: 1 is NOT prime because it only has one factor. 2 is the only even prime number. To check if a number is prime, try dividing it by primes up to its square root.

notes.heading: Prime Factor Trees
notes.body: Prime factorisation breaks a number into a product of prime numbers. Use a factor tree: split the number into two factors, then split again until every branch ends in a prime. Example: 60 = 6 × 10 = (2 × 3) × (2 × 5) = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5. Write the same primes together using powers.

notes.heading: Divisibility Rules
notes.body: Quick checks: A number is divisible by 2 if it is even; by 3 if the digit sum is divisible by 3 (e.g., 126: 1+2+6=9, so divisible by 3); by 4 if the last two digits form a number divisible by 4; by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5; by 9 if the digit sum is divisible by 9; by 10 if it ends in 0. These help find factors quickly without a calculator.

notes.heading: HCF and LCM
notes.body: HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the largest factor shared by two numbers. LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) is the smallest multiple shared. Method 1: list factors or multiples. Method 2: use prime factors. For HCF, multiply the lowest power of each common prime. For LCM, multiply the highest power of every prime that appears. Example: 36 = 2² × 3² and 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. HCF = 2² × 3 = 12. LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 180.

flashcards.definition: A whole number that divides exactly into another number with no remainder.
The result of multiplying a number by a whole number.
A number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
flashcards.example: 7 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 7.

flashcards.definition: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers.
Highest Common Factor: the largest factor shared by two or more numbers.
Lowest Common Multiple: the smallest multiple shared by two or more numbers.
A number made by multiplying a whole number by itself.
A quick way to decide if one number divides exactly into another.
flashcards.example: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

questions.stem: Which of these is a factor of 36?
questions.explanation: 36 ÷ 9 = 4 exactly, so 9 is a factor. The other options leave a remainder.

questions.stem: Which list shows all the factors of 18?
Which number is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 2, and it is the smallest prime.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a prime number?
questions.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, so it has more than two factors and is not prime.

questions.stem: What is the first multiple of 6 that is greater than 20?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, ... The first one after 20 is 24.

questions.stem: Which number is divisible by both 2 and 3?
questions.explanation: 24 is even so divisible by 2, and 2+4=6 which is divisible by 3.

questions.stem: What is the HCF of 24 and 36?
questions.explanation: Factors of 24: 1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24. Factors of 36: 1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36. The highest common is 12.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6: 6,12,18,24,30,... Multiples of 8: 8,16,24,32,... The lowest common multiple is 24.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorisation of 30?
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All factors must be prime, and 1 is not prime.

questions.stem: Which number is a square number?
questions.explanation: 36 = 6 × 6, so 36 is a square number. The others are not products of a whole number times itself.

questions.stem: Using divisibility rules, which number is divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: For 234, digit sum is 2+3+4=9, which is divisible by 9, so 234 is divisible by 9.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 30 and 45 using prime factors.
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 and 45 = 3 × 3 × 5. Common primes are 3 and 5, so HCF = 3 × 5 = 15.
